title: Unstable CPU usage with minimal project
body: ### Tested versions v4.7.rc3.official [645638db9] v4.7.rc2.official v4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4] ### System information w11 ### Issue description Ryzen 5600x 16 gb ram 1650 gtx Hi, honestly I have no idea if this is a bug, I've never seen Godot behave like this before, and I've been using it since version 3.2. I simply press the down arrow key, the object hits the floor (This sometimes helps to trigger these strange spikes, but it is not strictly necessary to do so.), and I click the mouse buttons randomly, which triggers these performance spikes... It seems strange to me; I don't recall Godot ever behaving this way in previous versions. Also, when I stop the execution, Godot sometimes freezes for about 3 seconds. 2 videos: Embedded mode: https://youtu.be/oBVw7klqq7k Non-embedded mode: https://youtu.be/hMB-bjxgTGc?si=Tb3-7KDuI1m4ojZ3 Version 4.6.3 test project: Minimal 2D project 256x240 resolution Capped at 60 FPS Maybe related https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/113501 Edit: Now, all of a sudden, it’s working normally again without any performance spikes. After testing different Godot versions and switching the renderer to 'gl_compatibility' and back to 'mobile', it's working normally... I don't understand what happened. ### Steps to reproduce Execute. Move the mouse around the game window and click the mouse buttons randomly (I'm not sure if this is related, but it seems to help trigger the performance spikes and that highly unstable consumption line). ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28989248/test.zip)
